chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever visits a sick person, Allah — Mighty and Majestic — assigns an angel with him, visiting him in his grave.

key_terms.عَادَ مَرِيضاً: visiting a sick person ('iyadah al-marid) — a communally recommended act in Islamic law
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave — the place of the barzakh, where the soul remains until resurrection
key_terms.مَلَكاً: an angel — a celestial being assigned as a companion and blessing
key_terms.وَكَّلَ: assigned/allocated — God's direct action of entrusting an angel for this purpose

ai.seo_question: What reward does Islam promise for visiting a sick person according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that visiting the sick (a practice known as 'iyadah) carries an immense spiritual reward: God assigns a dedicated angel to accompany the visitor in his own grave. This hadith frames an act of social compassion as a form of worship with eschatological consequences, encouraging believers to fulfill this communal obligation. The promise of angelic companionship in the grave resonates deeply with early Muslim concerns about the isolation and trials of the barzakh (intermediate realm).

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who visits a sick one, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Allocate an Angel with him, visiting him in his grave’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam from certain individuals of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one visits a patient, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, assigns an angel to visit him in his grave.”
